title: Per-user Econ Configurator — scratchpad
content:
Purpose: rough ideas for a per-user economic configurator — a lightweight UI + API that lets apps tune cost/latency/quality tradeoffs at the user or cohort level. This is an internal notes scratchpad: lots of half-formed ideas, questions, and quick acceptance criteria.

Top-level problem we want to solve:
- Apps want predictable per-user spending envelopes and the ability to map user segments to different inference profiles (fast-cheap vs high-fidelity).
- Today customers either configure per-route/global settings or build bespoke middleware. That is error-prone and hard to iterate on.

Goals (high level):
1) Make it trivial to set per-user (or per-cohort) budget/priority profiles.
2) Expose sensible defaults and safe fallbacks so apps don't accidentally blow budget.
3) Keep the runtime routing simple: policies should compile to routing directives we already support (model variant, batch priority, KV caching ttl, quantization tag).
4) Give visibility: cost forecasts, needle alerts (user TTLs near exhaustion), and post-facto per-user cost breakdowns.

Who benefits:
- PLG apps wanting freemium vs paid feature gating by per-interaction cost.
- Customer success teams creating curated experiences for pilot customers.
- Platform teams wanting rate-limited, tiered inference budgets per identity.

Surface ideas (UI + API):
- UI: "Econ Configurator" page. List of user cohorts + Active policy. Quick-edit inline to change: monthly_token_budget, per-session_token_cap, default_fidelity (low/med/high), allow_tools (bool), response_timeout_ms (soft).
- API: POST /v1/policies (scope: user|cohort|route), GET /v1/policies?user_id=..., PATCH /v1/policies/:id. Policy JSON is small: {name, scope, matchers, token_budget_monthly, session_token_cap, fidelity_tier, fallback_policy_id}.
- SDK helpers: client-side hooks to query effective policy for a user (cache TTL 60s) so frontend can show remaining credit.

Policy compilation -> runtime mapping (sketch):
- fidelity_tier -> model_variant (gptx-4-lite / gptx-4 / gptx-4-high-fidelity), quantization profile suggestion, decoding temp and top_p presets.
- token_budget_monthly -> accounting hook + throttling: if a user is above threshold, policy resolves to economy_fidelity and hard per-session cap applied.
- session_token_cap -> runtime enforcer: cap tokens for generation request; returns structured response with 'truncated_by_quota':true.

User stories (rough):
- As a product manager, I can define a "trial" cohort with monthly_token_budget=200k and default_fidelity=low so free users get capped cheap responses.
- As an engineer, I can query a user's policy in the SDK and preemptively show a warning if their session will be capped.
- As a CS rep, I can create an "enterprise pilot" cohort that maps to dedicated model variants and higher burst allowances.

Edge UX flows and messages:
- If a request is truncated due to session cap: return 206-like payload + header X-Redwood-Quota-Reason: session_cap_exceeded and a small suggestion card: "Upgrade to X to get full response".
- Soft degrade flow: when monthly budget is near exhaustion, automatically enable progressive-slimming (reduce verbosity, reduce top_k) before switching model variant. Show telemetry.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- UI to create/edit policies scoped to user/cohort (CRUD).
- Backend policy storage + simple matcher (email domain, user_id list, feature flag) for 3 match types.
- Compilation pipeline that outputs runtime directives (model_variant, session_cap_tokens, batch_priority).
- Runtime respects session_cap_tokens in generation path and logs events to cost telemetry.
- Basic billing report that aggregates cost per user and shows budget burn rate.

Metrics to track:
- % requests served under policy-derived economy mode vs baseline.
- Average tokens per session for each cohort.
- Budget exhaustion events per 1k users.
- False positives where policy mis-applies (mismatched matchers).

Open questions / risks:
- How fine-grained should matchers be? Freeform boolean expressions add power but complexity. MVP: user_id list, email domain, numeric cohort id, feature_flag.
- Storage and propagation: policies changing should have TTL and propagate quickly to edge (enforced at call-time). We can use a hot cache with 30s invalidation. But what about immediate revocation? Manual revoke could take up to cache TTL. Acceptable for MVP.
- Charging: do we bill differently by fidelity? We can map unit cost multipliers to model_variant; product/billing team needs to align.
- UX friction: surfacing remaining tokens per user could invite gaming or privacy concerns. Provide opt-in or admin-only.

Experiment ideas (week 1–4):
Week 1: implement API + small storage + CLI to apply policy to single user. Collect telemetry on token enforcement.
Week 2: add SDK query helper + simple UI list for policies; run internal pilot with 5 internal users.
Week 3: trial with one PLG customer (Dev sandbox) to get feedback on messaging and tolerances.
Week 4: open beta, collect metrics, tune default_fidelity profiles.

Implementation roadmap (very rough):
- Backend: policy store (Postgres table), matcher eval (SQL-ish), compile job -> directive blob.
- Cache: Redis with per-policy keys, 30s TTL.
- Runtime: hook into pre-generate path to enforce session cap and select model_variant.
- UI: minimal table + policy editor.
- Telemetry: cost events, truncated events, policy_applied tags.

Notes / UX copy ideas for messages:
- "You're on a limited plan: this response was shortened to keep your monthly budget on track. Upgrade to unlock full answers."
- Admin console flag: "Send in-product tip when users hit 80% of budget"

Next steps (for me):
- Spike schema for policy JSON (30m).
- Draft wireframe for UI (draw.io).
- Sync w/ billing PM: do we have per-variant cost multipliers? (Mira)
- Get runtime eng slot to review enforcement path (Devon)

Quick spike notes (schema idea):
- policy_id: uuid
- name: string
- scope: user|cohort|global
- matchers: [{type: 'email_domain', value: 'acme.com'}] (MVP: list only)
- token_budget_monthly: int|null
- session_token_cap: int|null
- fidelity_tier: low|medium|high
- fallback_policy_id: uuid|null

Random thoughts:
- Could integrate with Optimize recommendations: auto-suggest session caps based on historical token burn per user.
- Consider 'grace credits' for invites/referrals to avoid immediate truncation for first session.
- Make sure telemetry tags policy_id so we can slice costs in Console.

End of scratchpad. This is intentionally rough — will flesh after initial engineer sync.
